stem:
Calcitriol is a steroid hormone found in human blood.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give the number of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohol groups in one molecule of calcitriol.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Give the number of chiral carbon atoms in one molecule of calcitriol.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Calcitriol shows geometrical isomerism.

Give the number of geometrical isomers of calcitriol, including calcitriol.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Predict the number of peaks in the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of **X**.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: For the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of **X**, state the expected chemical shift ranges ($\delta$) of the peaks predicted in (i) and the number of peaks in each range.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Predict the number of peaks this compound would show in its proton NMR spectrum.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: For each of the peaks in the proton NMR spectrum you have identified in (iii) give the expected splitting pattern. Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem: In addition to the product shown in (d), two other carbon-containing products are formed when a sample of calcitriol is treated with an excess of hot, concentrated, acidified potassium manganate(VII).
parts.text: Of these two other carbon-containing products, identify the product with the **smaller** molecular mass. Explain how this product is formed.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Of these two other carbon-containing products, identify the product with the **larger** molecular mass by drawing its skeletal formula in the space below.
